To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have measured the electromagnetic breakup cross section of 8Li on Pb and C targets and found that the nuclear breakup is the dominant component of the total breakup at grazing angles.
the angular distribution of the neutron breakup cross section for 8Li on Pb at 41 MeV/nucleon is similar in shape to the neutron capture cross section for 7Li(p,γ) 8Be at astrophysical energy.
the Coulomb dissociation of 8Li on Pb and C at 41 MeV/nucleon is a good approximation to the (n,γ ) reaction at astrophysical energy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement of Coulomb dissociation cross section for 8Li at intermediate energies and its comparison to the well established (n,γ ) cross section at astrophysical energy.
the development of a new technique to measure the astrophysical (n,γ)-reaction cross sections for neutron-rich unstable nuclei.
the development of a new method to measure the neutron-capture reaction cross sections at stellar energies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electromagnetic dissociation is the dominating process at forward angles, but the nuclear dissociation dominates the reaction cross sections above the grazing angle.
the nuclear contribution to the breakup of 8Li at the beam energy of 41 MeV/nucleon is not negligible.
the electromagnetic contribution is dominant for the Pb target at all angles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Coulomb breakup is the dominant process for the breakup reactions of 8Li.

Coulomb dissociation is a very promising tool for studying neutron-capture cross section at astrophysical energy, but it is necessary to take into account the nuclear contribution in the forward region.
the Coulomb dissociation is the dominant reaction for lead, while the nuclear dissociation dominates the carbon breakup.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Coulomb dissociation is a good tool for studying neutron-capture reactions, but the results have to be corrected for the nuclear contribution.
the nuclear contribution can be significant even at very forward angles and the Coulomb dissociation cross section can be significantly overestimated if the nuclear contribution is neglected.
it is not possible to determine the neutron capture cross section of 7Li from the 8Li breakup experiment alone.
